recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce an R4-style categorized artifact inventory into the current R6 ballot page unless a new ballot-specific request asks for it; the current page should remain tailored to the active ballot content.
issue_request: FHIR-14437 was a Published, Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core ballot-intro change request from the STU3/R4 ballot cycle. It asked that the ballot artifact listing distinguish pages, resource/type definitions, value sets, operations, and similar artifact classes instead of presenting a grab-bag list; the recorded resolution was for Grahame to organize it and fix duplicate names.
initial_application: No commit explicitly tagged FHIR-14437 or GF#14437 was found. The application appears in the unkeyed August 2018 ballot-intro cleanup sequence, especially commit 065dd60a02a46f92fdf88e8a78083031a88d469a, which organized source/ballot-intro.html under package and artifact-category headings such as Base Documentation, RESTful API, Operations, Data Types, Resources, CodeSystem, ValueSet, CapabilityStatement, and OperationDefinition.
additional_context: The current active ballot-intro page is an R6 ballot roadmap, not the old STU3/R4 comprehensive artifact listing. It remains in build scope through publish.ini and source/hierarchy.xml, but its current change details are organized as scope notes, moved resources, other moved artifacts, and specific requests for balloter attention. Zulip and Confluence searches found no discussion that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the requested historical categorization was applied for the relevant ballot cycle, and the current R6 ballot-intro source is not misleading in the way FHIR-14437 described.
